findings.claim: As of the latest leaderboard snapshot (2026-05-17), Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is the top open <=1B multilingual embedder on MTEB Multilingual (MMTEB), and the overall #1 is Tencent's KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3-12B-2511 — meaning the sub-1B crown has NOT moved since June 2025, so a new sub-600M model has a stable, beatable target.
findings.numbers: Sub-1B: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 64.34 Mean(Task); multilingual-e5-large-instruct 63.22 (560M); EmbeddingGemma 61.15 (308M); bge-m3 59.56 (568M); jina-embeddings-v3 58.37 (570M). Overall: KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3-12B-2511 72.32 (11.76B, 3840d); Qwen3-Embedding-8B 70.58; Qwen3-4B 69.45; llama-embed-nemotron-8b 69.46.
findings.relevance: Defines the exact score-to-beat table for the paper's embedding deliverable in the <=600M class.

findings.claim: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B full spec: 28-layer decoder (Qwen3 base), last-token [EOS] pooling, 1024-dim output, 32K context, instruction-aware (instruction concatenated into query input). Training: (1) ~150M weakly-supervised synthetic pairs generated by Qwen3-32B across 4 task types (retrieval, bitext, classification, STS) with controlled query type/length/difficulty/language; (2) SFT on ~19M pairs (~7M labeled: MS MARCO/NQ/HotpotQA/MIRACL/MLDR/CodeSearchNet + ~12M synthetic filtered at cosine>0.7); (3) slerp model-merging of fine-tuning checkpoints. Loss: InfoNCE with in-batch negatives, K hard negatives, and false-negative masking (negative masked if its similarity exceeds positive-pair similarity by >0.1).
findings.numbers: MTEB Multilingual: 64.33/69.45/70.58 for 0.6B/4B/8B; MTEB English v2: 70.70 for 0.6B. 150M weak pairs + 19M SFT pairs.
findings.relevance: The reference recipe if the Kazakh embedder shares the decoder SLM backbone; every component (synthetic pairs from own LLM, cosine filtering, slerp merge, FN masking) is directly copyable at 10-100x smaller scale.

findings.claim: EmbeddingGemma (308M = ~100M transformer + ~200M embedding params) is the best open model under 500M on MTEB Multilingual v2. Recipe: encoder initialized from T5Gemma (encoder-decoder trained from Gemma 3, giving bidirectional context), mean pooling, 768d with MRL truncation to 512/256/128, geometric embedding distillation from Gemini Embedding (teacher), spread-out regularizer, model souping over domain-specialized checkpoints, and QAT for sub-200MB RAM inference.
findings.numbers: 61.15 MTEB Multilingual v2 mean, 250+ languages, 768d->128d MRL, <200MB RAM after QAT.
findings.relevance: Proof that a ~300M model with distillation from a large teacher reaches near-1B quality; T5Gemma-style encoder init from your own decoder SLM is the architecture bridge between the two deliverables.

findings.claim: CRITICAL: the newest small decoder-based embedders COLLAPSE on low-resource languages while old XLM-R-based mE5 holds up. On a native Armenian benchmark (zero-shot): Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B averaged 47.38 and EmbeddingGemma-300m 52.43 vs multilingual-e5-base 64.30, mE5-large 72.11, mE5-large-instruct 72.99. AfriMTEB/AfriE5 independently found E5-family outperforming EmbeddingGemma and Qwen3-0.6B on African LRLs. Cause: XLM-R's CC100 pretraining + tokenizer cover LRLs; the new models' synthetic contrastive data skews to high-resource languages.
findings.numbers: Armenian avg: Qwen3-0.6B 47.38, EmbGemma 52.43, mE5-base 64.30, mE5-large-it 72.99 (Table 1). MMTEB rank order (Qwen3-0.6B 64.34 > mE5-large-it 63.22) INVERTS on LRLs.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.22290 (Less is More, Mar 2026, Table 1); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.23896 (AfriMTEB/AfriE5)
findings.relevance: The headline MMTEB leaderboard is misleading for Kazakh; the real bar is mE5-large-instruct-class models plus adapted variants, and this inversion is the paper's core motivation for a Kazakh-native embedder.

findings.claim: 'Less is More' (arXiv 2603.22290, Mar 2026) shows the cheapest known path to a SOTA LRL embedder: fine-tune mE5-base on just 10k NOISY synthetic pairs (English Reddit title-body machine-translated by Gemma-2-27B-it) -> +11-12% average, retrieval +35% relative, matching 1M-pair training. Scaling 10k->1M adds <1%; translation quality and domain diversity don't matter; 0.5/0.5 weight-averaging with the base model prevents catastrophic forgetting (+2-8 pts). Filtering: drop pair if |sim(q_en,p_en) - sim(q_lrl,p_lrl)| > 0.05 or translation similarity < 0.85 (measured with mE5). Setup: full FT, effective batch 512, lr 7e-5, 5 epochs; 10k pairs cost <$20 via Gemini Flash.
findings.numbers: mE5 Armenian: retrieval 58.15->79.35, avg 64.30->76.42 (merged) with 10k pairs; 1M pairs gives 79.02 avg (no gain). EmbeddingGemma under same protocol: 52.43->67.19 at 10k but needs 1M to reach 77.06 — encoders adapt more data-efficiently than decoder-derived embedders.
findings.relevance: Drop-in protocol for a day-one Kazakh baseline AND the strongest competitor your final model must beat; also defines the data-filtering recipe for all synthetic kk pairs.

findings.claim: The Less-is-More authors explicitly flag as UNTESTED whether noisy-alignment holds for 'languages sharing a script with a high-resource neighbor (e.g., low-resource Cyrillic languages), where token overlap might change the adaptation dynamics' — Kazakh (Cyrillic, heavy kk/ru code-switching) is exactly this case, and it is an open, publishable research question.
findings.numbers: Validated only on Armenian (hye) and Georgian (kat), both unique-script isolates; Georgian: MTEB[kat] 71.02->77.18 with same 10k protocol.
findings.relevance: A ready-made experimental contribution for the paper: replicate their 10k/50k/1M ablation on Kazakh and characterize how ru-script overlap changes alignment — novel either way it turns out.

findings.claim: VERIFIED by running the mteb library locally (July 2026): MTEB contains exactly 16 Kazakh tasks, of which only 11 are text-embedding-relevant: 5 bitext mining (Flores, NTREX, Tatoeba, WebFAQ QAs/Questions), 3 classification (SIB200Classification.v2, CyrillicTurkicLangClassification, TurkicClassification), 1 clustering (SIB200ClusteringS2S), 2 retrieval (BelebeleRetrieval, WebFAQRetrieval). There is ZERO Kazakh STS, zero pair classification, zero reranking, and zero native QA retrieval — KazQAD is NOT integrated into MTEB.
findings.numbers: 16 tasks total (incl. 5 audio/any2any); 2 text retrieval tasks, 0 STS, 0 reranking.
findings.source: mteb PyPI package, mteb.get_tasks(languages=['kaz']), verified locally 2026-07-03
findings.relevance: This is the concrete missing-benchmark bottleneck: 'best Kazakh embedder' cannot currently be demonstrated on MTEB — building kk-MTEB tasks is a mandatory roadmap milestone, not optional.

findings.claim: KazQAD (ISSAI, LREC 2024) is the only native Kazakh retrieval benchmark: ~6,000 unique questions (NQ-translated train + original Kazakh UNT exam dev/test), ~12,000 passage-level relevance judgments, 800k+ Kazakh Wikipedia passages. Published retrieval baselines are weak: NDCG@10 = 0.389, MRR = 0.382 — large headroom for a Kazakh-native embedder. CC BY-SA licensed.
findings.numbers: 6k questions, 12k qrels, 800k passages; NDCG@10 0.389, MRR 0.382; reading comprehension EM 38.5 / F1 54.2.
findings.relevance: Ready-made retrieval eval + training qrels for the Kazakh embedder; converting it to an MTEB task is a cheap, high-visibility contribution.

findings.claim: KAZ-QA-RAG (2025) benchmarked BM25, BGE-M3, Arctic-Embed, E5, LaBSE, and text-embedding-3-large on KazQAD-style retrieval and reports Arctic-Embed as the best retriever for Kazakh (best pair: KazLLM-8B + Arctic-Embed); exact Recall@k/MRR numbers are in their artifacts, not the README.
findings.numbers: No per-model numbers visible in the repository README.
findings.relevance: Names the specific off-the-shelf models to include in the paper's Kazakh baseline table; Arctic-Embed L 2.0 must be in the beat-list.

findings.claim: BGE-M3 (568M, XLM-R-large): unified tri-head model — dense (1024d CLS), learned sparse lexical weights, and ColBERT-style multi-vector — trained with self-knowledge distillation where the sum of the three heads' scores forms the teacher distribution; 8192-token context (query 512/passage 8192 in pretraining); SOTA-at-release on MIRACL multilingual retrieval; ~1.2B weakly-supervised pairs then fine-tuning.
findings.numbers: 568M params, 1024d dense, 100+ languages, 8192 ctx; MMTEB mean 59.56.
findings.relevance: The hybrid dense+sparse+multi-vector design is especially attractive for agglutinative Kazakh, where learned sparse lexical matching can compensate for morphological variation that hurts dense-only retrieval.

findings.claim: KaLM-Embedding-V2 (HIT/Tencent) is the closest architectural template to the project's plan: Qwen2-0.5B decoder converted to a bidirectional-attention encoder with mean pooling, 896d with MRL (896/512/256/128/64), 32k context. Recipe: weakly-supervised pretraining on 20 data categories -> SFT on 100 categories -> model-soup averaging; innovations: focal-style reweighting of hard examples and ONLINE hard-negative mixing (no offline mining cost). SOTA under 1B on MTEB(cmn,v1) and MTEB(eng,v1). The same team's Gemma3-12B version is now MMTEB #1 (72.32), proving the recipe scales.
findings.numbers: 0.5B params, 896d, 32k ctx; MMTEB #1 overall for the 12B sibling at 72.32.
findings.relevance: Direct proof that a ~500M decoder SLM (like KazLLM-v2's backbone) converts into a top-tier embedder via bidirectional attention + mean pooling + 2-stage contrastive — the shared-backbone strategy in the project goal is validated practice.

findings.claim: Granite Embedding Multilingual R2 (IBM, 2026, Apache 2.0): ModernBERT-style encoders (alternating attention, RoPE, FA2) at 311M (768d, Gemma-3 262k tokenizer) and 97M (384d, pruned 180k vocab), 32K context, 200+ languages (52 retrieval-tuned). MTEB Multilingual Retrieval: 65.2 (311M, #2 open <500M; EmbeddingGemma 62.5, mE5-base 52.7) and 60.3 (97M, best sub-100M). Recipe: distillation from Granite/Mistral instruct teachers -> contrastive fine-tune -> model merging -> MRL (256d costs only -0.5 nDCG).
findings.numbers: 311M: 65.2 MTEB-Multilingual-Retrieval; 97M: 60.3 (+9.4 over mE5-small 50.9); 32K ctx; MRL to 128d.
findings.relevance: Shows a 97-311M ModernBERT encoder with a big-vocab tokenizer is the current efficiency frontier — and that vocabulary choice (their Gemma-3 262k vs your 50K Unigram kk-optimized) is a first-class design lever.

findings.claim: mmBERT (JHU, Sep 2025): ModernBERT-architecture multilingual encoder pretrained on 3T tokens covering 1,833 languages via 'annealed language learning' — 1,700+ low-resource languages are added ONLY in the final 100B-token decay phase (with inverse mask-ratio schedule and inverse temperature sampling), which 'boosts performance dramatically' on them; first encoder to beat XLM-R. Phases: 2.3T pretrain (60 langs) -> 600B mid-train at 8192 ctx (110 langs) -> 100B decay (1,833 langs).
findings.numbers: 3T tokens, 1833 languages, 8192 ctx, base ~307M.
findings.relevance: Two uses: (a) mmBERT-base is the freshest open encoder backbone to contrastively tune for Kazakh; (b) its decay-phase finding maps onto the SLM pretraining plan — concentrated kk exposure late in training is disproportionately effective.

findings.claim: Arctic-Embed 2.0 (Snowflake, Dec 2024): M 305M and L 568M multilingual retrievers with MRL applied at a single truncated dim of 256 during BOTH pretraining and fine-tuning, plus quantization-aware embedding training, enabling ~128 bytes/vector at high quality; strong on MTEB-R (55.6), MIRACL (55.8), CLEF (52.9/54.3) without sacrificing English — and per KAZ-QA-RAG it is the empirical leader on Kazakh retrieval among off-the-shelf models.
findings.numbers: 305M/568M; MRL-256 + int quantization = 128 bytes/vector (~4x compression); MIRACL 55.8.
findings.relevance: Its train-time single-dim MRL + quantization trick is the cheapest way to make the Kazakh embedder RAG-deployable on modest hardware (relevant for Kazakhstan-market adoption claims).

findings.claim: WebFAQ (96M natural QA pairs, 75 languages, 49% non-English) and WebFAQ 2.0 (198M pairs, 104-108 languages, hard negatives mined via BM25 top-200 -> BGE-M3 reranking) include Kazakh — MTEB's WebFAQRetrieval task has a kaz split — making it the largest known source of NATURAL (non-synthetic) Kazakh paired training data. Caveat from WebFAQ 2.0: with MNR contrastive loss, random negatives often beat their mined hard negatives due to false negatives; hard negatives helped mainly via MarginMSE distillation.
findings.numbers: 96M pairs/75 langs (v1); 198M/104-108 langs (v2); every language has >=1,000 samples; exact kk count not published in the papers' tables.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20936; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.17327v1; mteb WebFAQRetrieval task (kaz split verified locally)
findings.relevance: Primary natural kk pair source for stage-1 contrastive training; the false-negative caveat directly informs the negative-sampling design (prefer online mixing / FN-masking over naive offline mining).

findings.claim: Recipe convergence across ALL 2025-2026 top small embedders (Qwen3-Embedding, EmbeddingGemma, KaLM-V2, Granite R2, Arctic 2.0): (1) multi-stage training — weakly-supervised contrastive pretraining on massive pairs, then supervised fine-tune with hard negatives; (2) InfoNCE with in-batch negatives and false-negative handling; (3) checkpoint merging/souping (slerp or averaging) as a free robustness gain; (4) MRL; (5) instruction-prefixed inputs; (6) distillation from a larger embedder/LLM teacher. No top model skips more than one of these.
findings.numbers: 6/6 components in Qwen3 & Granite R2; EmbeddingGemma adds QAT; KaLM-V2 adds focal reweighting + online hard-negative mixing.
findings.relevance: This is the de-facto standard checklist the paper's embedding training spec should implement (and reviewers will expect); deviations need justification.

findings.claim: Competitor scan side-finding: two 2026 arXiv papers already target Kazakh SLMs — 'SozKZ: Training Efficient Small Language Models for Kazakh from Scratch' (2603.20854) and 'KazByte: Adapting Qwen models to Kazakh via Byte-level Adapter' (2603.27859); neither appears to ship an embedding model, so the embedding deliverable remains unclaimed territory, but the generative track's 'first/novel' claims must cite and differentiate from them.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.20854; https://arxiv.org/html/2603.27859 (titles/abstracts surfaced in search; full contents not fetched — outside embed domain)
findings.relevance: Novelty-positioning risk for the overall paper; the embedding gap strengthens deliverable (2) as the differentiator.

recommendations: Build the mE5 'killer baseline' first (1 GPU-day, <$50): translate 10k Reddit title-body pairs to Kazakh with a strong open LLM, filter with mE5 cosine-consistency (|sim_en - sim_kk| <= 0.05, translation sim >= 0.85), full-FT multilingual-e5-base (batch 512, lr 7e-5, 5 epochs), then 0.5/0.5 weight-average with the base. Per arXiv 2603.22290 this matches 1M-pair training and will likely beat every off-the-shelf embedder on Kazakh — it is both the strongest baseline your final model must beat and a sanity floor for the whole embedding track.

For the shared-backbone embedder, copy the KaLM-Embedding-V2 conversion exactly (proven on a Qwen2-0.5B, same size class as KazLLM-v2): enable bidirectional attention, mean pooling, then 2-stage contrastive training (weakly-supervised pairs -> supervised FT), with online hard-negative mixing + focal reweighting instead of offline mining (WebFAQ 2.0 showed offline-mined negatives often lose to random negatives due to false negatives), Qwen3-style false-negative masking (mask negatives scoring >0.1 above the positive), slerp checkpoint merging, MRL heads at {768/512/256/128/64}, and instruction prefixes.

Roadmap milestone M1 — 'kk-MTEB': MTEB today has only 11 Kazakh text tasks with ZERO STS, reranking, pair-classification, or native QA retrieval (verified via mteb lib). Ship: (a) KazQAD as an MTEB Retrieval task (data exists, CC BY-SA — mostly an integration PR to embeddings-benchmark/mteb, instant citability); (b) kk-STS: LLM-translate STS-Benchmark (~8.6k pairs) + native-speaker-verify a 1-3k subset + author 200-500 native pairs covering kk/ru code-switching (Armenian precedent: 3k translated STS + 185 manual gold pairs was enough for a credible benchmark); (c) a reranking task from KazQAD's 12k graded qrels.

Training-pair sourcing plan for the paper's data section: WebFAQ/WebFAQ 2.0 kk subset (largest natural kk pairs — quantify the exact count from the HF dataset as a paper table) + KazQAD train qrels + translated Reddit pairs + Qwen3-style synthetic pairs from your own generative SLM across 4 task types (retrieval/bitext/classification/STS) with cosine>0.7 filtering. Total needed is small: LRL alignment saturates near 10k-100k pairs for encoders, so budget goes to quality/diversity, not volume.

Claim a research contribution for free: run the Less-is-More 10k/50k/100k/1M ablation on Kazakh to answer their explicitly-open question — does noisy synthetic alignment hold for a Cyrillic LRL whose script overlaps a high-resource neighbor (Russian)? Tie the analysis to your tokenizer-fertility work (token overlap with ru is the hypothesized confounder). Publishable regardless of outcome.

Define 'best Kazakh embedding model on the market' operationally in the paper: beat, on kk-MTEB + KazQAD (baseline NDCG@10 = 0.389), all of: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (MMTEB 64.34 but LRL-weak), multilingual-e5-large-instruct (the real LRL threat, 560M), BGE-M3, Arctic-Embed L 2.0 (reported KazQAD leader), EmbeddingGemma-308M, Granite R2 311M, AND your own mE5+10k-kk adapted baseline. Beating only the leaderboard names without the adapted-mE5 control is the reviewer attack vector.

Adopt Arctic-2.0-style deployment compression: apply MRL at a single truncated dim (256) during both training stages plus quantization-aware embedding training, targeting ~128 bytes/vector — supports an on-device/cheap-RAG story for the Kazakhstan market and mirrors EmbeddingGemma's sub-200MB positioning.

Differentiators no incumbent has: (a) kk-Cyrl <-> kk-Latn (2031 transition) bitext augmentation so the embedder is script-invariant; (b) kk/ru code-switched pairs (use the 2026 '100,000+ Movie Reviews from Kazakhstan' corpus, arXiv 2605.08600, for natural code-switched text); (c) morphology-aware hard negatives (same lemma, different case/possessive suffixes) to exploit the agglutinative structure multilingual tokenizers mangle.
open_questions: Exact count of Kazakh QA pairs in WebFAQ/WebFAQ 2.0 (papers only guarantee >=1,000 per language; needs direct inspection of the PaDaS-Lab HF dataset) — determines whether natural kk pairs alone suffice for stage-1.
Exact per-model Recall@k/MRR on KazQAD from KAZ-QA-RAG (README has no numbers; need their paper or exp1_retrieval.py artifacts) to confirm Arctic-Embed's claimed lead on Kazakh.

Whether the live HF MTEB leaderboard (vs the codesota 2026-05-17 mirror) shows any newer sub-1B multilingual entrant as of July 2026; KaLM-Gemma3-12B-2511 at 72.32 #1 and Qwen3-0.6B at 64.34 sub-1B top should be re-verified on huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard before the paper's camera-ready.
Does Qwen3-Embedding's 119-language training coverage explicitly include Kazakh? The paper never names it; per-language MMTEB scores for kaz tasks would quantify the incumbent's true Kazakh strength.
Contents of SozKZ (2603.20854) and KazByte (2603.27859) — outside the embed domain but they gate the generative track's novelty claims; a separate subagent should fetch both.

Whether an mmBERT-base (307M ModernBERT, 1833 langs) contrastive fine-tune would beat the shared-backbone decoder conversion on Kazakh — the Armenian evidence (encoders more data-efficient on LRLs) suggests yes at equal params; worth a controlled experiment before committing to single-backbone purity.

research.area: embed-kazakh: Kazakh/Turkic embedding & retrieval landscape and bottlenecks (July 2026)

findings.claim: MTEB/MMTEB contains NO dedicated Kazakh task: no Kazakh STS, no NLI/pair-classification, no reranking, no KazQAD, and MASSIVE (MassiveIntent/MassiveScenario) has no kk subset. Kazakh appears only inside multilingual tasks: BelebeleRetrieval (kaz_Cyrl), WebFAQRetrieval (kaz-Cyrl), SIB200Classification + SIB200ClusteringS2S (kaz_Cyrl), TurkicClassification (kk news), CyrillicTurkicLangClassification, and bitext-mining tasks (FLORES, NTREX, Tatoeba, WebFAQ).
findings.numbers: grep of mteb main branch (July 2026): 13 task files mention kaz; 0 files mention KazQAD; 0 hits for kk in massive_intent_classification.py
findings.relevance: The paper can claim 'first Kazakh-native MTEB benchmark suite' as a deliverable; every missing task type is a concrete milestone.

findings.claim: Current best scores on the main public Kazakh retrieval signal, BelebeleRetrieval kaz_Cyrl→kaz_Cyrl (nDCG@10, official mteb results repo): Qwen3-Embedding-8B 0.956; BGE-M3 0.9017; multilingual-e5-large-instruct 0.8949; multilingual-e5-large 0.8269; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 0.7545; EmbeddingGemma-300m 0.6839. In the ≤600M class the bar is BGE-M3 (568M); the same-size Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is ~15 points behind it on Kazakh.
findings.numbers: nDCG@10: 0.956 (8B) / 0.9017 (BGE-M3) / 0.8949 (e5-large-instr) / 0.8269 (e5-large) / 0.7545 (Qwen3-0.6B) / 0.6839 (gemma-300m); crosslingual e5-large: kaz→eng 0.9255, eng→kaz 0.7881
findings.relevance: Defines the exact victory condition for deliverable (2): beat BGE-M3 0.9017 at ≤600M and approach the 8B's 0.956.

findings.claim: WebFAQRetrieval-kaz is the second public Kazakh retrieval task: multilingual-e5-large scores nDCG@10 0.7269; the WebFAQ corpus contains ~12.5k Kazakh QA pairs (of 96M pairs / 75 languages total).
findings.numbers: e5-large WebFAQ-kaz nDCG@10 = 0.7269; kaz subset = 12.5k QA pairs
findings.relevance: Second eval axis plus 12.5k natural kk QA pairs usable as fine-tuning data (dev/test hygiene needed to avoid train-test leak).

findings.claim: KazQAD (ISSAI) is the only real Kazakh ODQA/IR dataset: ~6,000 unique questions, ~12,000 passage-level qrels, corpus of 800k+ Kazakh Wikipedia passages, plus 61k machine-translated Natural Questions triples. Splits in issai/kazqad-retrieval: 3,487 train / 548 val / 1,929 test queries. Published retrieval baseline is weak: NDCG@10 = 0.389, MRR = 0.382. It is NOT integrated into MTEB.
findings.numbers: 6k questions; 12k qrels; 800k passages; 61k MT-NQ triples; baseline NDCG@10 0.389 / MRR 0.382; reading comprehension EM 38.5 / F1 54.2
findings.relevance: Primary supervised retrieval train/test set AND the hard-negative mining corpus (800k passages); contributing it to MTEB is a free paper milestone.

findings.claim: The only dedicated Kazakh embedder found is Nurlykhan/kazembed-v5: multilingual-e5-base (278M) fine-tuned on just 61,255 pairs (KazQAD 6,640 + KazQAD-Retrieval 44,615 + Powerful-Kazakh-Dialogue 10,000) with MultipleNegativesRankingLoss; KazQAD test Hits@1 72%, Hits@5 96%, MRR 0.835 (+2.1% MRR over base e5). No MTEB evaluation, no STS/clustering eval, 289 downloads. No from-scratch Kazakh embedding model exists anywhere.
findings.numbers: 278M params; 61,255 training pairs; MRR 0.835; Hits@1 0.72; Hits@5 0.96
findings.relevance: This is the entire 'dedicated competition' — a small fine-tune. Beating it and BGE-M3 makes the 'best Kazakh embedder on the market' claim defensible.

findings.claim: A Kazakh text-embedding leaderboard named KazTEB exists in name (HF Space batyrme/kazteb, indexed by Google) but returns 401/private as of 2026-07-03; the author has no public embedding models or benchmark datasets. There is currently NO operational public Kazakh embedding leaderboard.
findings.numbers: HTTP 401 on space page, API, and raw files; author's public artifacts: 1 unrelated ASR dataset
findings.relevance: Confirms the benchmark vacuum; the paper's MTEB(kaz) suite + leaderboard becomes first-of-kind, but check the space's content before claiming novelty in print.

findings.claim: No Kazakh STS or NLI dataset exists anywhere: XNLI's 15 languages exclude kk; MUSTS (ACL 2025, the broadest multilingual STS benchmark, 13 languages) verified to not contain Kazakh (full-text check of the PDF); HF dataset API searches for 'kaznli', 'nli kazakh', 'sts kazakh', 'kazsts' all return zero results. The closest artifact is Arailym-tleubayeva/KazakhTextDuplicates (10k-100k, duplicate/plagiarism detection, Mar 2025).
findings.numbers: 0 kk STS datasets; 0 kk NLI datasets; XNLI = 15 langs without kk; MUSTS = 13 langs without kk
findings.relevance: Biggest single benchmark gap — an embedder cannot even be evaluated on kk semantic similarity today; building KazSTS is a mandatory milestone.
findings.source: aclanthology.org/2025.acl-short.27 (PDF text extracted); huggingface.co/api/datasets searches 2026-07-03; XNLI arXiv:1809.05053

findings.claim: Zero Kazakh rerankers exist: HF search for 'kazakh reranker' returns no models; no cross-encoder trained on KazQAD is published.
findings.numbers: 0 results on huggingface.co/api/models?search=kazakh%20reranker
findings.relevance: A kk cross-encoder reranker trained on KazQAD + mined negatives is a cheap first-mover deliverable that also improves hard-negative mining for the embedder.

findings.claim: Parallel data for contrastive pretraining: KazParC = 371,902 human-translated parallel sentences across kk/en/ru/tr (CC BY 4.0, largest human-quality kk corpus). OPUS kk-en totals ~35.66M pairs but is dominated by noisy mined NLLB v1 (34.59M) + CCAligned (690k) + XLEnt (162k). OPUS kk-ru is surprisingly thin: only ~771k pairs (MultiCCAligned 432k) despite pervasive kk-ru code-switching in the wild.
findings.numbers: KazParC 371,902; OPUS kk-en 35,661,293 total (NLLB 34,589,761; CCAligned 689,653; XLEnt 161,706); OPUS kk-ru 771,081 (MultiCCAligned 431,953)
findings.relevance: Stage-1 weakly-supervised contrastive data exists at ~35M scale (needs margin filtering); the kk-ru pair shortage means code-switch pairs must be constructed, not downloaded.

findings.claim: Kazakh Wikipedia has 244,167 articles (668,261 pages) as of 2026-07-03 — the source of KazQAD's 800k-passage corpus — usable for ~0.5-1M synthetic title-lead/section-title/query-passage pairs and as the hard-negative mining pool.
findings.numbers: 244,167 articles; 668,261 pages; 800k+ passages in KazQAD corpus
findings.relevance: Only large clean monolingual pair source for synthetic query generation (doc2query with the project's own generative SLM closes the loop between the two deliverables).

findings.claim: Existing kk classification/clustering eval resources that can seed MTEB(kaz): KazSAnDRA sentiment (180,064 reviews, 1-5 ratings; best baseline F1 0.81 polarity / 0.39 score), Belebele kaz_Cyrl (900 questions), SIB200 kaz_Cyrl (~205 sentences, 7 topics), TurkicClassification kk news (e5-large accuracy 0.516), CyrillicTurkicLangClassification (8 Turkic languages).
findings.numbers: KazSAnDRA 180,064; Belebele-kaz 900; SIB200 ~205/lang; e5-large TurkicClassification kk = 0.516
findings.relevance: Enough raw material for classification/clustering tracks of a Kazakh MTEB suite without new annotation; only STS/reranking/retrieval-beyond-wiki need building.
findings.source: arXiv:2403.19335 (KazSAnDRA); embeddings-benchmark/results TurkicClassification.json; mteb repo task files

findings.claim: Kazakh instruction/dialogue pair data is small and mostly machine-translated: AmanMussa/kazakh-instruction-v2 (10k-100k self-instruct, updated Feb 2026), saillab/alpaca_kazakh_taco (10k-100k, MT Alpaca), DarkyMan/powerful-kazakh-dialogue (~10k) — roughly 100-150k instruction pairs total.
findings.numbers: ~100-150k instruction pairs across 3 datasets, all size-tagged 10K<n<100K
findings.relevance: Usable as instruction-tuning pairs for an instruct-embedder head, but quality audit needed (MT artifacts).

findings.claim: issai/RAGBench_Kazakh (Apr 2026) is a machine-translated Kazakh port of RAGBench: 11,431 test examples in 12 domain subsets (TatQA 3,258, FinQA 2,144, PubMed/CUAD/customer-support etc.), question+documents+answer format, CC-BY-4.0 — the first kk RAG-grounding eval, but 100% MT with English-origin domains.
findings.numbers: 11,431 examples; 12 subsets
findings.relevance: Free end-to-end RAG eval for the combined SLM+embedder demo chapter; its MT nature is itself a citable bottleneck (no native kk RAG benchmark).

findings.claim: Russian embedders do not cover Kazakh: FRIDA (ai-forever) and ru-en-RoSBERTa are ru/en models; Giga-Embeddings developers explicitly recommend it 'only for Russian'. None claims or benchmarks kk despite the shared Cyrillic script and heavy kk-ru code-switching — cross-script transfer from ru embedders to kk is unmeasured anywhere.
findings.numbers: 0 kk claims across FRIDA / Giga-Embeddings / ru-en-RoSBERTa model cards
findings.relevance: The kk-ru code-switching niche is completely unserved — a code-switch eval + training pairs is a differentiating milestone no competitor addresses.

findings.claim: Kaz-RoBERTa-conversational (kz-transformers) is the strongest monolingual kk encoder backbone: base-size RoBERTa pretrained from scratch on 25GB of Kazakh + kk-ru code-switched telecom dialogues, 52k BPE tokenizer, MLM objective (technical report Oct 2025). No sentence-embedding training was ever applied to it.
findings.numbers: 25GB corpus; 52k BPE vocab; base size (~125M)
findings.relevance: Useful ablation baseline (monolingual encoder + contrastive FT) against your decoder-backbone embedder; also evidence that code-switched kk-ru pretraining data exists.

findings.claim: Realistic total Kazakh pair budget for training: ~550-650k human-quality pairs (KazParC 372k + KazQAD 73k incl. MT-NQ + WebFAQ 12.5k + instructions ~100-150k) + ~0.5-1M synthetic Wikipedia pairs + ~5-8M usable mined bitext after margin-filtering the 34.6M NLLB kk-en pairs. This is 10-50x less supervised data than SOTA English/Chinese embedder recipes, which is why distillation from a strong multilingual teacher is structurally necessary.
findings.numbers: ~0.6M clean + ~1M synthetic + 5-8M filtered mined = ~7-10M usable pairs
findings.relevance: Directly sizes the two-stage contrastive training plan and justifies the teacher-distillation design choice in the paper.
findings.source: Aggregated from arXiv:2403.19399, arXiv:2404.04487, PaDaS-Lab/webfaq, OPUS API, HF dataset metadata (this survey)

findings.claim: 289 sentence-transformers models on HF are tagged kk, but the top-downloaded ones are all generic multilingual models (multilingual-e5 family, gte-multilingual-base, granite-embedding-r2, jina-clip-v2, plus 2026 releases microsoft/harrier-oss and codefuse F2LLM-v2-0.6B); a comparative study of embedding models for kk question-context matching exists (ResearchGate 396213005) but is 403-blocked.
findings.numbers: 289 tagged models; multilingual-e5-large 12.2M downloads
findings.relevance: Confirms 'Kazakh support' today means passive inclusion in multilingual training, never kk-optimized; the 2026 models (harrier-oss, F2LLM) should be added to the baseline table after verification.

recommendations: Make 'MTEB(kaz)' an explicit paper deliverable: submit a PR to embeddings-benchmark/mteb adding (a) KazQADRetrieval from issai/kazqad-retrieval (1,929 test queries, 800k-passage corpus — already IR-formatted), (b) KazSAnDRA polarity classification, (c) the new KazSTS, and register them as a Benchmark preset so the public leaderboard renders a Kazakh tab. This converts the benchmark vacuum into a citable first-of-kind contribution and makes the 'best on market' claim externally verifiable.

Build KazSTS because none exists: (a) test set — professionally translate + culturally adapt the 1,379-pair STS-B test into kk, then re-score with 3 native annotators (report Krippendorff's alpha), plus ~1.5k native pairs sampled from kk news/wiki/social for domain balance; (b) training data — machine-translate XNLI train (393k pairs) kk→ via Tilmash/NLLB with label-preservation filtering. Human annotation only for the test split keeps cost at roughly 3k pairs.

Two-stage contrastive training spec (drop-in): Stage 1 weakly supervised on ~7-10M pairs = NLLB kk-en margin-filtered from 34.6M to ~5-7M + CCAligned 690k + MultiCCAligned kk-ru 432k + ~1M Wikipedia title-lead/section pairs (from 244k articles) + WebFAQ-kk 12.5k. Stage 2 supervised MNRL with hard negatives = KazParC 372k + KazQAD train 3,487 + 61k MT-NQ triples + ~100k instruction pairs + a Tilmash-translated MS MARCO subset; mine hard negatives as BGE-M3 top-100 hits minus qrels over the 800k KazQAD wiki passages.

Distill from Qwen3-Embedding-8B (Kazakh Belebele nDCG@10 0.956, the ceiling) via similarity-distribution KL distillation, and adopt BGE-M3-style self-knowledge-distillation to co-train dense + learned-sparse heads on the shared ≤600M backbone. The learned-sparse (SPLADE-style over your 50k Unigram vocab with <2.0 fertility) head is the principled fix for agglutinative-morphology BM25 failure — quantify it against the published KazQAD BM25 baseline (NDCG@10 0.389).

Set exact victory thresholds in the paper: Belebele kaz_Cyrl-kaz_Cyrl nDCG@10 ≥ 0.93 (beats best ≤600M model BGE-M3 at 0.9017; within 2.6 pts of the 8B teacher), KazQAD test nDCG@10 ≥ 0.55 and MRR ≥ 0.87 (vs KazEmbed-v5 0.835), WebFAQ-kaz nDCG@10 ≥ 0.80 (vs e5-large 0.7269). Include Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (0.7545) and EmbeddingGemma-300m (0.6839) in the baseline table to show same-size dominance.

Train the first Kazakh reranker as a cheap milestone: cross-encoder (or the same backbone with a reranking head) on KazQAD qrels + Stage-2 mined hard negatives; zero kk rerankers exist, and it doubles as the labeling model for iterative hard-negative refresh.

Add a kk-ru code-switching retrieval eval (~500 real queries from kk forums/social with mixed-script passages) as a milestone: OPUS kk-ru is only 771k pairs, Russian embedders (FRIDA/Giga-Embeddings) explicitly do not cover kk, and no benchmark measures code-switched retrieval — this is an unserved niche your kk-ru-aware tokenizer directly targets.

Close the loop between the two deliverables: use the generative SLM for doc2query-style synthetic query generation over the 800k-passage wiki corpus (and kk news title-body pairs) — this is the standard fix for the ~10-50x supervised-pair deficit vs English recipes and gives the paper a clean 'one backbone, two products, mutual bootstrapping' narrative.

Before camera-ready, verify two post-cutoff artifacts: the private KazTEB space (contact author batyrme — avoid a novelty-claim collision) and the 2026 multilingual embedders tagged kk (microsoft/harrier-oss, codefuse/F2LLM-v2-0.6B) which may need to enter the baseline table.
open_questions: What is inside the private KazTEB HF space (batyrme/kazteb) — does it already define Kazakh embedding tasks that would collide with or complement the paper's MTEB(kaz) claim?
Do the 2026-released embedders tagged kk (microsoft/harrier-oss family, codefuse F2LLM-v2-0.6B, granite-embedding-r2) report Kazakh-specific scores anywhere, and where do they land on Belebele-kaz?
What is the actual noise rate of the 34.6M NLLB kk-en mined pairs after margin filtering (needs a 1k-pair manual audit to size Stage-1 data honestly)?
Does SemEval-2024 SemRel/STR or any 2025-2026 SemEval task include Kazakh STS (believed no, not verified)?
Content of the 403-blocked comparative study of embedding models for Kazakh question-context matching (ResearchGate 396213005) — does it establish baselines the paper must cite?
Is issai/kazqad-retrieval's negative-passage set sufficient for reranker training, or are its negatives too easy (BM25-sampled), requiring fresh dense-mined negatives?

research.area: decoder-to-embedder: turning the ~500M Kazakh backbone into a SOTA embedder (joint vs post-hoc vs adapter), benchmark landscape, and morphology effects

findings.claim: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is the model to beat in the 0.6B class. It is initialized from Qwen3-0.6B-Base (same generative-backbone-to-embedder pattern we propose), uses last-token [EOS] pooling with instruction-aware queries, supports Matryoshka dims 32-1024 and 32K context, Apache 2.0. Its recipe: Stage 1 weak supervision on ~150M synthetic multilingual pairs generated by Qwen3-32B; filter to ~12M high-quality pairs (cosine >0.7) for supervised Stage 2; then slerp model merging across checkpoints.
findings.numbers: MMTEB multilingual mean(task) 64.33; MTEB English v2 70.70; MTEB Code 75.41. No per-language Kazakh number is published anywhere — the on-Kazakh comparison is wide open.
findings.relevance: Defines both the recipe template and the concrete target: beat 64.33-class models ON KAZAKH, where no number exists yet — we must build the benchmark that measures it.

findings.claim: GRIT (GritLM-7B) proves one model CAN do both generation and embedding with no loss at 7B: joint training matched generative-only and embedding-only specialists, and unification speeds up RAG >60% on long documents via KV-cache reuse. Ablations show the failure of NOT training jointly: a generative-only 7B scores only ~41.2 on MTEB; an embedding-only model generates at random (~25 MMLU).
findings.numbers: GritLM-7B: MTEB 66.8 + generative avg 55.5; RAG speedup >60%; joint training needs ~2x batch memory (interleaved gen+emb batches).
findings.relevance: The strongest argument FOR a single shared backbone — but all evidence is at 7B, not 500M.

findings.claim: Counter-evidence at OUR scale: Hydra (2026) ran a controlled ablation of GritLM-style joint training at 0.8B and 4B and found joint training matched retrieval-only on retrieval but its generation mode COLLAPSED (in their LoRA setting). Their fix is the adapter pattern: base weights stay byte-for-byte identical for generation (426/426 tensors), a LoRA (r=32) switches the model into retrieval mode.
findings.numbers: 59.1% peak-GPU-memory reduction at 0.8B (5.79GB to 2.37GB) vs running two models; generation exactly preserved.
findings.source: arXiv 2603.28554 (Hydra: Unifying Document Retrieval and Generation in a Single Vision-Language Model)
findings.relevance: Directly answers the paper's key question at ~500M scale: full GRIT joint training is risky below 1B; a retrieval LoRA/adapter on the frozen generative backbone gets unification benefits without gambling the generative deliverable.

findings.claim: LLM2Vec is the cheapest post-hoc conversion and has numbers AT SMALL SCALE: S-LLaMA-1.3B reaches MTEB 49.42 unsupervised (bidir + MNTP + SimCSE) and 61.96 supervised. MNTP costs only 1000 steps on one A100; SimCSE ~2.5h (7B). Crucially, enabling bidirectional attention WITHOUT training hurts most models (except Mistral), and mean pooling beat EOS/last-token pooling across all their models.
findings.numbers: S-LLaMA-1.3B: 49.42 unsup / 61.96 sup MTEB; Mistral-7B: 56.80 unsup. MNTP: 1000 steps, batch 32, 1xA100-80GB.
findings.relevance: Sets the realistic ceiling for pure post-hoc conversion at ~1B: 61.96 supervised — below Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B's 64.33. Post-hoc conversion alone will not win; it needs the Qwen3/KaLM-style data pipeline on top.

findings.claim: Echo embeddings (repeat input twice, mean-pool second occurrence) improve zero-shot decoder embeddings by >5% and nearly match bidirectional-converted models with zero architecture change — but double sequence length/cost. Same paper confirms last-token pooling degrades sharply as input length grows; mean pooling wins by a wide margin for causal LMs.
findings.numbers: +5% zero-shot over classical LM embeddings; 2x inference cost.
findings.source: arXiv 2402.15449 (Repetition Improves Language Model Embeddings, ICLR 2025)
findings.relevance: Useful as a zero-training baseline row in our ablation table and as evidence against naive last-token pooling for an agglutinative language with long words/sentences.

findings.claim: Causal2Vec keeps the causal mask untouched (no surgery on the generative backbone): a tiny BERT-style pre-encoder compresses the input into one Contextual token prepended to the decoder; the embedding is concat(last hidden of Contextual token, EOS token). SOTA among models trained only on public retrieval data, while cutting sequence length up to 85% and inference time up to 82% vs echo-style methods.
findings.numbers: MTEB 66.10 vs 65.87 for best bidirectional method under identical training data.
findings.relevance: The most backbone-friendly conversion for a shared generative+embedding model: no attention-mask change means the generative weights and the Engram/mHC architecture stay intact.

findings.claim: NV-Embed's latent-attention pooling (512 latents, 8 heads) beats both mean and last-token pooling, and its two-stage instruction tuning (stage 1: retrieval with in-batch negatives; stage 2: blend non-retrieval tasks, disable in-batch negatives) was the recipe that set the MTEB record at 69.32 (v1, Mistral-7B base).
findings.numbers: MTEB 69.32 (NV-Embed-v1); pooling: 512 latents / 8 heads.
findings.relevance: Latent-attention pooling is a cheap add-on head (~few M params) worth ablating against mean pooling on the 500M backbone; the two-stage negatives schedule is directly copyable.

findings.claim: E5-Mistral's synthetic-data recipe is fully replicable for Kazakh: 500K synthetic examples with 150K unique instructions across 93 languages, generated 25% by GPT-3.5-Turbo and 75% by GPT-4 via two-step prompting (brainstorm task list, then generate query/positive/hard-negative triplets), then plain contrastive fine-tuning.
findings.numbers: 500K examples, 150K instructions, 93 languages; +2.4 MTEB points over prior SOTA at the time.
findings.source: arXiv 2401.00368 / ACL 2024 (Improving Text Embeddings with Large Language Models)
findings.relevance: Kazakh has almost no native paired data — synthetic generation with a strong teacher is the main way to manufacture the missing contrastive corpus.

findings.claim: KaLM-Embedding proves a 0.5B decoder (Qwen2-0.5B — our exact size class) can be a top multilingual embedder: causal mask removed, then three stages — weakly-supervised contrastive pretraining (20 data categories), high-quality SFT (100 categories), and contrastive distillation from fine-grained soft teacher signals. V2 outperforms all models under 1B on MTEB and rivals models several times larger.
findings.numbers: Backbone 0.5B; V2 beats bge-multilingual-gemma2 (9B) on Chinese tasks; MIT license.
findings.relevance: Existence proof for deliverable (2) at 500M — and its contrastive-distillation stage is the single highest-leverage technique to copy.

findings.claim: Kazakh is essentially ABSENT from MTEB/MMTEB as a first-class language: a code search of the mteb repository finds no KazQAD task and no Kazakh-native retrieval/STS/reranking task — Kazakh appears only via multilingual spillover (SIB-200 classification/clustering, FLEURS, Common Voice, Tatoeba bitext, WebFAQ, Turkic/Cyrillic-Turkic language-ID classification). There is no Kazakh STS dataset at all (SemRel2024's 14 languages exclude Kazakh; no KazSTS exists).
findings.numbers: 0 Kazakh-native retrieval, STS, or reranking tasks in mteb as of 2026-07.
findings.source: gh code search of github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb (kaz-Cyrl, KazQAD); arXiv 2502.13595 (MMTEB); arXiv 2402.08638 (SemRel2024)
findings.relevance: THE critical bottleneck: 'best Kazakh embedder' is currently unfalsifiable. Building kkMTEB is a mandatory milestone and a citable contribution in itself.

findings.claim: KazQAD is ready-made raw material for the retrieval part of kkMTEB: ~6,000 questions, ~12,000 passage-level relevance judgments, 800K+ Kazakh Wikipedia passages; published baselines are weak (BM25/neural retrieval NDCG@10 = 0.389, MRR = 0.382; ODQA EM = 17.8).
findings.numbers: 6K questions, 12K qrels, 800K passages; NDCG@10 0.389.
findings.relevance: Drop-in retrieval benchmark + hard-negative mining source + the headroom (0.389 NDCG@10) shows how beatable current Kazakh retrieval is.

findings.claim: Multilingual embedders underperform on Kazakh today: a 2025 comparative study on ~7,700 Kazakh question-context pairs (informatics domain) found LaBSE, multilingual-e5-small, GTE-multilingual-base, mMiniLM and Arctic-Embed v2.0 reach only Accuracy@1 of 0.59-0.63 vs 0.50 for TF-IDF — a thin margin over a lexical baseline.
findings.source: ResearchGate publication 396213005 (Comparative Analysis of Embedding Models for Matching Questions and Contexts in the Kazakh Language, 2025); dataset Kundyzka/informatics_kaz
findings.relevance: Quantifies the gap a Kazakh-specialized embedder can exploit; also a reusable eval set.

findings.claim: ruMTEB is the best construction template for kkMTEB: 23 datasets across 7 task types, 17 newly created from native sources (reviews, maps, science) + 6 from multilingual MTEB, with cleaning/filtering. Their specialized model ru-en-RoSBERTa (404M encoder, tokenizer extended with English tokens, MLM + slerp anti-forgetting, then InfoNCE with 7 hard negatives, temp 0.02) scores 61.77 vs mE5-large 61.41 and BGE-M3 61.58 — winning overall but LOSING retrieval/reranking to BGE-M3.
findings.numbers: 23 tasks / 7 types / 17 new; 61.77 vs 61.41 (mE5-large) vs 61.58 (BGE-M3).
findings.relevance: Both a benchmark blueprint and a warning: a ~400-500M specialized model only marginally beats multilingual giants unless retrieval training data is strong. Also relevant for kk/ru code-switching: they deliberately kept the second language (English there, Russian for us) in the tokenizer and data.

findings.claim: TR-MTEB (closest Turkic analogue) is a second warning: 26 Turkish datasets, 6 task types, a corpus of 34.2M weakly supervised Turkish pairs, contrastive pretraining + SFT — yet the Turkish-specialized models remained only 'competitive' and did NOT robustly surpass multilingual E5. Monolingual specialization with weak pairs alone does not win; pair quality and distillation matter more than pair count.
findings.numbers: 26 datasets; 34.2M weak pairs; specialized models do not beat mE5 overall.
findings.relevance: Calibrates our claim: 'beating all multilingual embedders on Kazakh' requires the AfriE5/KaLM distillation lever, not just scraped weak pairs.

findings.claim: AfriE5 shows targeted low-resource adaptation DOES beat the giants: cross-lingual contrastive distillation from instruction-tuned mE5 achieved state-of-the-art on AfriMTEB (59 languages, 14 tasks, 38 datasets), outperforming Gemini-Embedding and mE5 itself.
findings.relevance: The proven playbook for our situation: distill a big teacher's embedding space into the Kazakh-specialized student using kk and kk-ru parallel text (KazParC) as the bridge.

findings.claim: Morphology-aware tokenization measurably helps sentence-level semantics in agglutinative languages: for Korean, hybrid morpheme-segmentation-then-BPE beat pure BPE on KorSTS/KorNLI (AACL 2020); for Turkish/Finnish, linguistically informed segmentation improves embedding-space semantic coherence and OOV compositionality; for Kazakh specifically, the CSE-guided framework (Complete Set of Endings + vowel-harmony-aware FEMSeg-CRF, SentencePiece fine-tuned on CSE-segmented corpus) cuts neural training time ~33% via shorter sequences. No one has yet ablated morphology-aware tokenization on Kazakh EMBEDDING quality — that experiment is free novelty for us.
findings.numbers: ~33% training-time reduction for Kazakh CSE-guided tokenization; Korean hybrid morpheme+BPE best on KorSTS (exception: pure BPE best on KorQuAD).
findings.source: arXiv 2010.02534 (Korean tokenization, AACL 2020); MDPI Information 17(2):128 Jan 2026 (Kazakh CSE-guided); github.com/walsher46/Kazakh-tokenizer; arXiv 2509.14238 (Turkish/Finnish); arXiv 2606.18717 (Morpheus)
findings.relevance: Supports the <2.0 fertility target AND motivates a tokenizer ablation (Unigram-50K vs CSE/morpheme-guided Unigram-50K) measured on kk-STS/KazQAD.

findings.claim: Matryoshka + quantization is a near-free market feature: int8 scalar quantization loses almost nothing (recall -1.46%, MRR -2.72% at 384d); pure binary is a cliff (-17% recall) but binary + float rescoring retains 95-96%; 2-bit/hybrid schemes recover 95-98% at >90% memory reduction. Qwen3-Embedding already ships MRL 32-1024, so parity requires it.
findings.numbers: int8: -1.46% recall; binary: -17%; binary+rescore: 95-96% retention; 2-bit: 95-98% at >90% memory saved.
findings.relevance: Train with MRL loss from the start and publish int8/binary retention numbers on kkMTEB — cheap differentiation for the 'best embedder on the market' claim.

findings.claim: Late chunking (encode whole document once with a long-context embedder, mean-pool per chunk afterwards) yields contextual chunk embeddings that improve long-document retrieval nDCG with NO extra training — but only works if the embedder has real long context.
findings.relevance: Argues for giving the embedding variant at least 8K context (backbone likely trains at 2-4K) so Kazakh RAG over long documents works out of the box.

findings.claim: There is NO established recipe that integrates a contrastive objective INTO LM pretraining at scale — GRIT, KaLM, Qwen3-Embedding all do contrastive work as a post-pretraining stage; the closest research is LLM-JEPA (joint-embedding predictive auxiliary objectives on LLMs, 2025), still exploratory. Meanwhile direct Kazakh SLM competitors exist as of 2026 — SozKZ (50M-600M Llama-style, 50K BPE, 9B kk tokens from scratch; 600M scores 30.3% on Kazakh cultural QA) and KazByte (byte-level adapter on Qwen) — but NEITHER touches embeddings.
findings.numbers: SozKZ-600M: 30.3% Kazakh cultural QA (vs Llama-3.2-1B 32.0%); 9B training tokens.
findings.relevance: Two implications: (a) a contrastive auxiliary loss during pretraining would be a novel but risky headline — frame it as an ablation, not the core bet; (b) the embedding deliverable is our clean differentiation from SozKZ/KazByte, who must now be cited and beaten on the generative side too.

open_questions: Does Hydra's small-scale finding (joint GRIT training collapses generation at 0.8B under LoRA) hold for full-finetune text-only models at 500M, or was it a LoRA artifact? Our GRIT-at-500M ablation would be the first clean answer — worth positioning as a paper contribution.

What does Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B actually score on Kazakh tasks (KazQAD retrieval, SIB-200 kk, a translated kk-STS)? Nobody has published this; we must measure it ourselves in week 1 — if it is already weak (like mE5's 0.59-0.63 Acc@1), the headline claim is very reachable.

How much kk paired data can a teacher LLM generate at acceptable quality — is Qwen3-32B/DeepSeek-class fluent enough in Kazakh to synthesize E5-style triplets, or do we need generate-in-Russian + translate-with-KazParC-trained-MT + native filtering?

Does the Engram n-gram memory + mHC residual architecture interact badly with bidirectional attention or latent-attention pooling (Engram lookups assume causal context)? If yes, Causal2Vec-style conversion (causal mask untouched) may be the only compatible option.

Can KazSAnDRA, Belebele-kk, KazNERD and Tatoeba kk-ru be cleanly licensed and reformatted into mteb task classes for upstream contribution, and will the mteb maintainers accept a kkMTEB PR (they accepted AfriMTEB and ruMTEB tasks)?
recommendations: ARCHITECTURE DECISION (answer to the key question): do NOT bet on full GRIT joint training at 500M. Ship two sibling artifacts from one backbone, Qwen3-style: (1) finish the generative model; (2) branch KazEmbed-500M from the final backbone checkpoint via a KaLM/Qwen3-style pipeline — remove/soften causal mask (or use Causal2Vec contextual-token to keep the mask and Engram intact), contrastive weak pretraining, then SFT, then contrastive distillation from Qwen3-Embedding-8B or Gemini-Embedding (the AfriE5 lever). Include a GRIT-at-500M joint-training run and a frozen-backbone retrieval-LoRA run as ablations — first published evidence at this scale.

POOLING SPEC: default to mean pooling (LLM2Vec + echo evidence: mean >> last-token for causal LMs, and last-token degrades on long agglutinative sentences); ablate NV-Embed latent-attention pooling (512 latents, 8 heads — only a few M params) and Causal2Vec concat(Contextual, EOS). Report all three on kk-STS/KazQAD.

DATA PIPELINE (the missing paired data milestone): (a) mine weak pairs from kk corpus — title/body, headline/article, QA forums, Wikipedia section/summary — target 10-30M pairs; (b) generate 300-500K E5-Mistral-style synthetic triplets in Kazakh with a strong teacher using the two-step prompt recipe (brainstorm tasks, then query/positive/hard-negative), with native-speaker spot-checks; (c) use KazParC kk-ru parallel data as bitext positives AND as the bridge for cross-lingual distillation from the teacher's Russian-strong embedding space; (d) filter everything at cosine >0.7 with mE5-large/LaBSE (Qwen3's exact filter).

BENCHMARK MILESTONE (must-reach, week 1-3): build kkMTEB following the ruMTEB recipe (23 tasks/7 types, 17 native): reuse KazQAD as the retrieval task + a reranking task from its qrels; KazSAnDRA (classification); SIB-200-kk + Belebele-kk (classification/comprehension); Tatoeba/KazParC kk-ru (bitext mining); CREATE kk-STS by machine-translating STS-B/STS17 (~3K pairs) with native-speaker verification of a 500-pair gold subset — none exists today. Upstream the tasks to github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb (they accepted ruMTEB and AfriMTEB) so external leaderboard numbers become citable.

BASELINE TABLE (run before training anything): evaluate Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, KaLM-Embedding-v2 (0.5B), multilingual-e5-large, BGE-M3, LaBSE, Arctic-Embed-v2 and BM25 on kkMTEB. This is the paper's Table 1 and de-risks the 'beat everything on Kazakh' claim early.

TRAINING SCHEDULE: copy NV-Embed's two-stage negatives curriculum (stage 1 retrieval tasks with in-batch negatives; stage 2 blend STS/classification/clustering tasks with in-batch negatives disabled) and Qwen3's slerp checkpoint merging; InfoNCE temp ~0.02 with 7+ mined hard negatives per query (ruMTEB values).

MRL + QUANTIZATION: train with Matryoshka loss (dims 64/128/256/512/768) and publish int8 and binary+rescore retention on kkMTEB (expect ~99% and ~95-96%); this matches Qwen3-Embedding's feature set and directly serves the 'cheap vector DB' market positioning.

TOKENIZER ABLATION (novel result): train the 50K Unigram tokenizer twice — statistical vs CSE-guided morpheme segmentation (walsher46/Kazakh-tokenizer + MDPI Information 17(2):128 method) — and measure BOTH generative (KazMMLU) and embedding (kk-STS, KazQAD nDCG@10) deltas.
